author: san jose standard
title: Golden Knights defeat Sharks after five-goal first period - San Jose Standard
text:
The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the San Jose Sharks 7-2 at T-Mobile Arena on Tuesday, scoring five goals in the first period. Thirteen Golden Knights players registered at least one point, and Mitch Marner led with two goals. The win ended a three-game losing streak for Vegas.
Golden Knights coach Bruce Cassidy commented on the team’s strong start: “Honestly, to be up 5-0 after one period is rare. You need everything to go right on both sides of the puck. That’s what I was as much pleased about is when it got to 2-0, maybe 3-0, we didn’t change the way we played. We didn’t give up much that first period, if anything.”
For San Jose, Macklin Celebrini and Collin Graf scored while Tyler Toffoli contributed two assists. Goaltender Yaroslav Askarov allowed four goals before being replaced by Alex Nedeljkovic late in the first period. “It wasn’t our night tonight,” Toffoli said. “‘Asky’ kept us in there as long as he could, but it felt like they had all the momentum and we had no pushback.”
Brett Howden opened scoring for Vegas less than two minutes into the game. Reilly Smith assisted with a lead pass that set up a 2-on-1 rush finished by Braeden Bowman and Howden. Marner made it 2-0 with a power-play goal at 9:07 after his shot deflected off Alexander Wennberg’s skate.
“A little bit of a lucky bounce,” Marner said.
Colton Sissons increased the lead to 3-0 following a quick transition play with Keegan Kolesar. “We were able to transition pretty quickly and get some breaks off the rush,” Sissons said. “‘Koley’ made a great play and found me an easy one on the backdoor, which hasn’t been coming all too easy this year, so I’ll take it.”
Tomas Hertl added another goal for Vegas at 14:57 after Ty Dellandrea turned over the puck to Pavel Dorofeyev, who found Hertl near the net.
Mark Stone scored late in the first period to make it 5-0.
Celebrini put San Jose on the board early in the second period with his 19th goal of the season.
Smith scored again for Vegas late in the second period before Marner added his second goal early in the third. “Great play by both the wingers,” Marner said. “[Ivan Barbashev] winning a board battle, going up the ice and making a great play to ‘Stoney,’ who hit me backdoor.”
Graf closed out scoring for San Jose by deflecting in a rebound from Toffoli.
“We’re .500 [37 games in], and that’s probably how we played,” Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky said. “There’s moments [that are] in the right direction. It feels like we take two steps forward, one step back.”
Celebrini extended his point streak to six games and tied Sidney Crosby’s record for most points by a teenager entering an NHL holiday break (55 points). The Golden Knights have now scored five goals in one period three times in franchise history; their last occurrence was against Chicago on February 27. Vegas also extended its point streak against San Jose to twelve games—tied for their third-longest run against any team.
